Subject: Meridian transfer questionnaire + signing cadence

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We got an initial request from our privacy team to reconcile data transfer approaches before procurement can move to signature. Two quick asks to help us align with our legal/compliance: 

1) Can Redwood provide a clear pairing recommendation: SCCs (standard EU SCCs) + UK IDTA (UK addendum) vs relying on a single TIA/DTIA for our EU+UK workloads? We need the path that minimizes operational changes for our ops team while satisfying the auditors.

2) We attached our short transfer questionnaire (Meridian_Transfer_Questionnaire.xlsx). Can you confirm which artifacts Redwood will provide (signed DPA redline, subprocessor list, SOC 2 + KMS attestation, transfer impact assessment) and an estimated delivery date?

3) Procurement needs a signing cadence — is a two-step (DPA now, addendum to follow) OK, or do you prefer a single DocuSign envelope that includes the UK addendum?

I'll loop in procurement if you want; Tom Hayes is our finance lead (cc'd on follow-ups).

Thanks,
Susan Park
Head of Privacy Programs
Meridian Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Meridian transfer questionnaire + signing cadence

Hi Susan — thanks for the questionnaire, looks straightforward. High level answers and proposed cadence below. I'm copying Kim (Legal) and Laura (Privacy) to confirm the legal/technical positions.

Summary recommendation (Redwood):
- Preferred: Execute a single DPA with the EU SCCs incorporated and the UK IDTA (UK Addendum) appended in the same DocuSign envelope. This reduces paperwork for both sides and is our standard for customers operating in EU+UK.
- Alternate: If procurement requires separation, we can sign the base DPA first and publish the signed UK Addendum within 3 business days after — this is operationally viable but increases back-and-forth.

Artifacts we will provide (deliverable schedule):
- Redwood DPA redline (internal) — draft to you by EOD tomorrow (Dec 2). [We will attach Redwood_DPA_Redline_for_Meridian.pdf].
- Current subprocessor list & dataflow mapping — shared link by Dec 3.
- SOC 2 Type II report summary + KMS attestation — redact-sensitive sections and provide by Dec 6.
- Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA/DTIA) summary — we'll provide a one-page TIA that maps to SCCs + UK addendum by Dec 6. If you need a full DTIA we can extend the timeline by one week.

Operational notes:
- If Meridian uses onshore-cache fallback in EU regions, we need to confirm whether the cache is treated as a subprocessor; generally yes. For on-prem or partner-hosted caches we require subprocessors to be named or covered by a scope carve-out.

Proposed signing cadence: single envelope with DPA + UK Addendum (preferred). If Meridian insists on stepwise signing, we'll accept DPA first with a separate follow-up addendum.

Next steps:
1) Kim/Laura: confirm legal stance on onshore-cache fallback and whether Redwood's existing UK Addendum language (standard) is acceptable.
2) Jordan: send redline and Drive link to artifacts (tomorrow).
3) Meridian: confirm preferred signing flow (single envelope vs two-step).

Best,
Jordan Blake
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Redline_for_Meridian.pdf]
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Meridian transfer questionnaire + signing cadence (legal comments)

Thanks Jordan — quick legal note from our side. I'm including the key redline points here so they appear in thread (I added inline comments in the PDF redline as well).

1) UK Addendum approach: We recommend the single-envelope approach, with the UK IDTA attached as an addendum. That aligns with our precedent and avoids signature mismatches across documents.

2) Subprocessors & onshore caches:
- If Meridian's architecture routes EU-origin data through a third-party onshore cache in the US, we treat that resource as a subprocessor. We can accept a conditional subprocessor list (i.e., allow named providers or a scoped statement) but require either (a) an explicit subprocessor addendum prior to activation, or (b) a documented fallback that disables the cache for EU-origin flows until the addendum is accepted.

3) Logs & escrow: Redwood does not typically place raw logs into escrow. We can provide a certified evidence package (audit extract + retention attestations) and, if needed, a time-bound transfer of redacted logs under escrow-like controls. That is heavier lift and will impact timeline and cost.

4) Security artifacts: We'll provide SOC 2 summary, encryption-in-transit and at-rest matrices, and KMS key custody attestation. If Meridian requires HSM-level proofs, that is an extra step and will need procurement clarity.

Please confirm whether Meridian's privacy team will accept the certified evidence package in lieu of full log escrow. If they require escrow, we need to scope that as a procurement change.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Redline_for_Meridian.pdf]

Appreciate the clear summary. A couple of procurement questions from my side: 

- DocuSign: We prefer a single envelope with DPA + UK Addendum. Can you confirm Redwood can route the envelope to our procurement and then to our CEO for final signature?
- SOC 2 + KMS: Our compliance gate requires a redacted SOC 2 Type II and a KMS attestation showing whether keys are customer-managed or Redwood-managed.
- Escrow: Meridian's data governance team asked whether any production logs (full request/response) could be escrowed as a last-resort for forensic access. From your legal note it sounds like you prefer an evidence package. Can you confirm whether evidence package + retention attestations are acceptable to our auditors?

If we get the DocuSign envelope and the attestation docs by next Wednesday (Dec 16), procurement will be able to push to signature before year-end.

Thanks — Tom
